newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria looks at second telecoms network.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria looks at second telecoms network.

text.p: Nigeria's military government believes a second telecommunications network is needed to compete with state-run Nigerian Telecommunications (NITEL), the communications minister said.

"It is our considered opinion that the current monopoly status of NITEL be removed to allow the introduction of a second carrier so as to open up the telecommunications sector and create a level playing field for full and fair competition," Major General Tajudeen Olanrewaju told a meeting of the "Vision 2010" economic think-tank on Thursday.
The government last year gave out several licences to companies offering services through the NITEL network and with mobile telephones. But so far only limited services are provided.
Olanrewaju said any second network operator would have to "include the provision for local, long distance and international communication...
"In order to meet the expansion target the second operator would be required to install a minimum of one million lines by the year 2005."
Africa's most populous nation has an exchange capacity of only around 600,000 for over 100 million people -- and most of the lines are not connected.
New subscribers can wait years for lines and when they get them find themselves cut off by bureaucratic inefficiency or heavy rain.
Telecommunications is one of the areas identified by the World Bank and local business as potentially benefitting most from privatisation.
But in his 1997 budget military ruler General Sani Abacha shied away from a quick sell-off.
